A survey from YouGov/Economist released on Tuesday shows that in a generic congressional vote, 36 percent of U.S. adults would pick the Democratic candidate compared to 31 percent who would pick the Republican candidate. One percent said other, eight percent said not sure and 23 percent said they would not vote.

The poll surveyed 1,592 U.S. adults from August 28-31 and had a margin of error of 3.5 percent. results.content: Other recent surveys have also pointed to a Democratic advantage on the generic congressional ballot. A YouGov/Economist poll found that 36 per cent of US adults would choose a Democratic candidate, compared with 31 per cent for a Republican candidate. [...] A separate Quantus Insights survey of likely voters put Democrats ahead 49.7 per cent to 42.8 per cent on the generic congressional ballot. The same poll showed Democrats leading Republicans 49.3 per cent to 43.4 per cent in a generic Senate ballot.

results.query: YouGov Economist survey US adults Democratic Republican lead

results.content: Democrats continue to have an edge over Republicans in vote intent for the November elections for U.S. Congress, according to the latest Economist / YouGov Poll. 46% of registered voters say they will vote for the Democratic Party candidate in their district, and 40% will vote for the Republican candidate. That 6-point Democratic lead among registered voters is in line with recent weeks, and larger than the Democrats' low-single-digit lead for much of the summer.
